articles.title: Perplexity, Burstiness, and AI Text Detection: An NLP Glossary
articles.excerpt: What do "perplexity," "burstiness," and "watermarking" actually mean when people throw them around in AI-detection debates? We wrote a plain-English glossary of the core NLP vocabulary, grounded in th…
articles.body: What do "perplexity," "burstiness," and "watermarking" actually mean when people throw them around in AI-detection debates? We wrote a plain-English glossary of the core NLP vocabulary, grounded in the primary papers. Here is the short version of the terms that matter most, with why each one is in the conversation. Perplexity Perplexity measures how "surprised" a language model is by a text: the average probability it assigns to each next token, inverted. Low perplexity means the text reads as highly predictable to a model. Because model-generated text tends to be fluent and statistically bland, detectors and researchers often treat very low perplexity as a machine-likeness signal.

articles.excerpt: Exploring graph-powered reasoning, MCP, and AI agents for the FalkorDB Graph Hacks hackathon. Imagine you're managing a distributed application with dozens of interconnected services. Suddenly, the In…
articles.body: Exploring graph-powered reasoning, MCP, and AI agents for the FalkorDB Graph Hacks hackathon. Imagine you're managing a distributed application with dozens of interconnected services. Suddenly, the Inventory Service fails. Will the Order Service be affected? Could Shipping experience downstream issues? Which business workflows might be disrupted? Finding these answers isn't always straightforward. In a system with many dependencies, understanding the potential impact of one failure can require tracing multiple relationships across the infrastructure. That's the problem I'm exploring with RIPPLE — AI What-If Impact Investigator, my project for Track 1: Agents That Act on Connected Data at the FalkorDB Graph Hacks hackathon .

articles.title: Is my Supabase database public? A 5-minute check with the anon key
articles.excerpt: If you shipped a Lovable (or any Supabase) app, your anon key is in the browser. That's fine, it's supposed to be. The real question is different: can a stranger read your tables with that key and no…
articles.body: If you shipped a Lovable (or any Supabase) app, your anon key is in the browser. That's fine, it's supposed to be. The real question is different: can a stranger read your tables with that key and no login? If Row Level Security is off on a table that still has grants to anon , the answer is yes. Here's a 5-minute check you can run on your own project. Why the anon key isn't the leak The anon key is a public JWT. Postgres then decides what it can do in two layers: Grants decide whether anon can SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE the table at all. RLS decides which rows survive that grant. RLS off means the second layer never runs. If anon also has a grant (the old default on public tables), every row is reachable from the REST endpoint.

articles.title: An ESP32 and a Local Vision Model Drive My iPhone
articles.excerpt: Apple spent 17 years convincing us that controlling an iPhone requires Xcode, a $99 developer account, and a that costs more than your couch. Henry Yuan spent $7 to prove them wrong. His repo — esp32-…
articles.body: Apple spent 17 years convincing us that controlling an iPhone requires Xcode, a $99 developer account, and a that costs more than your couch. Henry Yuan spent $7 to prove them wrong. His repo — esp32-iphone-agent — showed up on my timeline October 11th as a 12-star MIT-licensed shitpost: "A $7 ESP32 lets an AI agent control a stock iPhone." Hackaday picked it up Oct 14th. By the time I cloned it, it had 2,975 stars. You are still early. The trick isn't AI. It's hardware heresy. Yuan split the classic computer-use agent into three organs and built each from spare parts: Eyes: AirPlay mirroring Hands: An ESP32-S3 pretending to be a USB mouse and keyboard Brain: Any OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint No WebDriverAgent. No CoreDevice hack. No app on the phone that Apple has to sign.

articles.title: Repopilot : Platform to generate revenue off Side Hustle Projects
articles.excerpt: RepoPilot AI — code review that runs on your laptop, not someone else's GPU This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle RepoPilot AI is a local-first code r…
articles.body: RepoPilot AI — code review that runs on your laptop, not someone else's GPU This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built RepoPilot AI is a local-first code review assistant. You paste a unified git diff, and a small open-weight model running in Ollama on your own machine reviews every changed file: real defects only, each cited to its line number in the new version of the file, ranked high → medium → low. Who pays for it. Freelancers and small teams working under NDA. Every hosted review tool means uploading a client's source to someone else's servers, holding an API key, and paying per token. RepoPilot has no API key, no per-token bill and no upload — the code never leaves the laptop, and it keeps working offline.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
